display.title: Episode 449: Skippy and Crawly (Parshas Noach)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi draws living lessons from Parshas Noach, then tells of Skippy the grasshopper and Crawly the ant to show that effort brings success.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Parshas Noach 5751, with Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan on Shabbos. Uncle Yossi retells the story of the flood: the people stole and were cruel, and only Noach the tzaddik, his family and the animals were saved in the ark. Torah means 'teaching', so the story holds living lessons: Hashem created and runs the world, protects the righteous and provides for them, as we say in the second paragraph of the Shema; so learn Torah, do mitzvos, and read Parshas Noach in your own Chumash. After the Hakochainik march, a second-grade class from a Brooklyn girls' school recites the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: a father encourages his son Dovid, who is struggling in school, with the tale of Skippy the grasshopper, who plays all summer, and Crawly the ant, who stores food for winter. When the snow comes, Skippy has no food or shelter. Like the Torah's 'evening, then morning', hard work comes first and success follows. The show ends with an invitation to write about Hakafos, Shabbos candle times and Rosh Chodesh.
display.lesson: Work hard first, even when it is difficult, and success will follow; learn living lessons from the Torah.
